title: POC scoping - success criteria sign-off (Atlas Financial)
summary: Redwood and Atlas aligned on POC success criteria: p95 latency thresholds, throughput targets, qualitative correctness thresholds and reporting format. Agreed benchmark harness, representative workload (input length distribution, concurrency), and acceptance tests. POC duration ~3 weeks with security docs and benchmark results delivered for sign-off.
next_steps: Redwood to share benchmark harness config + runbook (link) by 2025-07-04
Atlas to provide representative prompt set (500) and expected labels by 2025-07-07
Schedule first benchmark run week of 7/14; Redwood to run hosted + dedicated variants
Redwood to share SOC2 and SSO docs by 2025-07-06
Follow-up call to review benchmark results on 2025-07-25
action_items: Maya Patel: Send benchmark harness config and test runbook (due 2025-07-04)
Jared Cole: Upload 500 representative prompts and acceptance labels to shared drive (due 2025-07-07)
Eric Huang: Prepare benchmark scheduling and resource plan for dedicated run (due 2025-07-10)
Liam O'Connor: Confirm security questionnaire fields and share any additional controls required (due 2025-07-06)
Sofia Ramirez: Draft POC report template for weekly delivery (due 2025-07-11)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intro, i'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account. we also have Eric our SE and Sofia from CS.
[00:08] Jared Cole: thanks Maya, Jared here. we wanted to lock down success criteria for the POC so we can sign off internally. we've got a timeline pressure - Q3 rollout pref so need clear go/no-go.
[00:20] Maya Patel: Totally. goal of today's call is to agree on measurable acceptance tests, workload sizing, benchmark plan, and reporting format. Eric do you want to lead the technical bits?
[00:30] Eric Huang: Sure. quick high level: we'll run three benchmark passes - hosted api baseline, dedicated reserved capacity, and a quantized model variant if needed. each pass will include cold-start and steady-state.
[00:40] Priya Nair: when you say "steady-state" - what's the concurrency target? our prod simulator runs around ~60 concurrent sessions for the use case, average prompt length 120 tokens in, expecting ~64 tokens generated.
[00:52] Eric Huang: OK that helps. for POC we'll mirror that distribution. proposed concurrency profile: ramp to 60 concurrent, hold for 10 minutes per run, repeated 3 times. total synthetic requests ~2k per run.
[01:05] Hannah Lee: we also care about cost - need a cost per 1M tokens estimate for each config so we can compare hosted vs dedicated.
[01:12] Maya Patel: absolutely. we'll include cost estimates per million tokens and per-request breakdown.
[01:18] Liam O'Connor: security stuff - SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs. we need to confirm Redwood's controls before we can accept results.
[01:25] Maya Patel: understood. we'll send our SOC2 pdf and the security pack. note that for private/VPC flows we can integrate with customer KMS; we'll include that in the docs.
[01:34] Eric Huang: back to acceptance criteria - proposed quantitative thresholds: latency: p95 generation latency <= 300ms for typical prompt+gen (note: 300ms here is for 128/64 typical; adjust for longer requests); throughput: sustain 60 concurrent sessions with <5% error rate; correctness: >= 88% pass rate on customer-labeled relevance/return-rate on the 500-sample prompt set (binary pass/fail rubric); hallucination: <5% hallucination rate by sample audit on 100 random outputs.
[01:58] Priya Nair: those latency numbers feel optimistic - we're used to p95 around 800ms with cloud endpoints. can you explain how Redwood expects 300ms?
[02:08] Eric Huang: good call - the 300ms is our target for an optimized path (GPU-backed model, sequence lengths like you specified). but we should make this explicit: separate thresholds for small/medium/large request classes. e.g., small (<=128 tokens total) p95 <= 300ms, medium (129-512) p95 <= 600ms, large (>512) p95 <= 1200ms.
[02:27] Jared Cole: ok that split makes sense. we will provide distribution so you can run weighted percentiles.
[02:33] Maya Patel: perfect. on quality we recommend a simple rubric the Atlas team maintains: relevant? accurate? risky/hallucination? mark as pass/fail. we'll run the rubric on your 500 prompts and a smaller 100 sample audit by Redwood.
[02:45] Hannah Lee: what's the acceptance pass threshold again?
[02:48] Eric Huang: we propose >=88% pass rate on the 500-sample set for go. for safety/hallucination the internal audit must be <5% hallucination.
[02:56] Liam O'Connor: and if we fail? what's the remediation path?
[02:59] Maya Patel: good question. remediation options: 1) tune model variant/temperature; 2) enable prefix caching or different quantization; 3) runway for additional tuning and re-run benchmarks - we recommend up to two re-runs within the POC window. final sign-off will be on the re-run if needed.
[03:13] Priya Nair: for reporting format - we need a CSV with row-per-request plus separate aggregated metrics. what columns would you include?
[03:20] Eric Huang: we'll deliver both: raw per-request CSV (request_id, timestamp, prompt_length, response_length, model_variant, latency_ms_p50/p95, error_flag) plus aggregated dashboard CSV (p50/p95 lat, throughput, token/sec, cost_per_1M_tokens, error_rate, pass_rate on labeled set).
[03:36] Hannah Lee: cadence? weekly report during POC and a final consolidated report?
[03:40] Sofia Ramirez: yes weekly reports every Monday, plus the final report within 3 business days of final benchmark. we'll include sample outputs and the labeled pass/fail sheet.
[03:50] Jared Cole: timeline - we have budget approval by mid-July. are you saying POC is 3 weeks?
[03:55] Maya Patel: recommended POC length: 3 weeks. week 1: integration + dry runs; week 2: hosted and dedicated baseline benchmarks; week 3: remediation and final runs + report.
[04:05] Liam O'Connor: what's the expected resource footprint for the dedicated runs? GPU type?
[04:09] Eric Huang: for the model family you're evaluating, we recommend an A100/RTX8000 equivalent for dedicated testing. we'll provide exact instance configs - also run a lower-cost quantized variant on T4 if you want cost vs perf comparison.
[04:23] Priya Nair: fine. one more item - availability SLO for dedicated: we need 99.9% target during reserved hours.
[04:29] Maya Patel: we can put that in the Dedicated contract. for the POC we'll track uptime during the run and include it in the final report.
[04:36] Hannah Lee: acceptable error modes? e.g., timeout vs degraded generation.
[04:40] Eric Huang: we'll classify errors into timeouts, model errors (decode failure), infra errors (503), and response quality failures flagged by rubric. each will be in the error breakdown.
[04:50] Jared Cole: on acceptance tests - can you put the go/no-go thresholds in a single acceptance table so our procurement and security teams can sign off?
[04:57] Maya Patel: yes we'll create a one-page acceptance matrix with thresholds and pass/fail criteria and attach to the SOW.
[05:03] Priya Nair: about the benchmark harness - will Redwood run it or we run it from our infra?
[05:07] Eric Huang: flexible. we can run from our infra to ensure identical environment across runs, or run from your environment if you prefer. we recommend Redwood-run for consistent comparability between hosted/dedicated.
[05:18] Jared Cole: ok Redwood-run is preferred. we'll still want to validate one run from our side.
[05:23] Maya Patel: noted. last piece, reporting to execs - we will include cost/latency tradeoff slides and recommendation: hosted for initial launch, dedicated for high-throughput steady-state.
[05:33] Hannah Lee: any blockers?
[05:35] Liam O'Connor: once we get SOC2 and KMS details, security is unblocked.
[05:38] Maya Patel: timeline recap: Maya to send harness by 7/4, Atlas to upload prompts by 7/7, first benchmark week of 7/14, reports weekly, follow-up 7/25 to review.
[05:48] Jared Cole: sounds good. thanks all.
[05:50] Maya Patel: thanks, we'll follow up in the CRM and share links.
[05:54] [call ends]
questions: How will Redwood measure hallucination rate?
Can we get a per-request CSV with model_variant and cost metrics?
Will the POC include private/VPC testing or only hosted/dedicated?
